paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when the pressure comes, Jesus answers with what God has said. Three times the devil comes at Him, and three times Jesus says, "It is written." He doesn't argue, He doesn't hype Himself up, and He doesn't make up a clever line. He stands on the Word of God, and that's where I want you standing too (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10).

Now look at HOW the devil comes at Him. He doesn't show up with a scary mask. He shows up with a Bible verse of his own, and that's the part that should make every one of us pay attention (Matthew 4:6). I think this is why knowing Scripture matters so much. If you only know a few verses, a twisted one can sound pretty good, but if you know the Word, you can tell when somebody is bending it.

And here's the good news, baker. Jesus was led by the Spirit into that wilderness, and when the tests were over, "the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him" (Matthew 4:1, 11). Temptation is real, but it doesn't get the last word. When your own wilderness shows up, remember that Jesus has already faced it with the Word, and every verse you hide in your heart is one more thing to stand on.
